clue.text: Style on The Independent, a means of making sparks fly

definitions.text: a means of making sparks fly

parts.note: touch means a distinctive manner or style, as in an artist's touch
The Independent is a newspaper, so a paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lively house style is said to set off fireworks among readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is an indicator: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second. A touchpaper is the fuse-paper lit to set off a firework.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting the blue fuse-paper of a firework sets it off, so it is literally what makes sparks fly.

clue.text: Licensed agent

definitions.meaning: an agent here is a person acting for an authority, a functionary

explanation.surface: A spy or representative holding a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something licensed is authorised or approved; an agent of an organisation is one of its functionaries or officers.

clue.text: Shot shore-bird right on the bottom

parts.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird of marshes and shores

explanation.surface: A wading bird has been shot in the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the bottom' puts R below SNIPE in this down entry. 'Shot' is a noun here: a marksman, as in 'a good shot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A good shot is a marksman, and a sniper is a marksman who shoots from hiding.

clue.text: Jetty ripe for demolition

indicators.note: a structure due for demolition is to be knocked down and rebuilt, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old jetty is ready to be pulled down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a landing stage built out over the water, much like a jetty.

clue.text: Emulsion paint put on new church in moderation

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: tempera is a paint made by mixing pigment with an emulsion such as egg yolk
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Decorating advice: apply emulsion to the new church sparingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places the paint above the rest in this down entry; 'in' is a link before the definition. Tempera is the paint artists bind with egg yolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance is self-restraint, especially in drinking, which is moderation.

clue.text: Misfortune I had when engulfed by stress

indicators.note: being engulfed means being swallowed up inside something, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the accent on a syllable is the stress put on it
I'd is the contraction of 'I had'

explanation.surface: Someone tells of a mishap suffered while overwhelmed by pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' looks like worry, but it is the stress laid on a syllable; 'when engulfed by' puts the contraction inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unlucky mishap, a piece of misfortune.

clue.text: Catbird, say, a cheeky creature in the garden

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male cat and a tit is a small bird, so a cat-bird pair

definitions.text: a cheeky creature in the garden
definitions.meaning: a small, bold songbird common at garden feeders

explanation.surface: A bird is described as a bold little visitor to the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a cryptic one: a tom is a cat, so a TOM TIT is literally a cat-bird. The catbird is also a real American songbird, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, tom and tit give a cat plus a bird; the tomtit is a small bold garden bird such as the blue tit.

clue.text: Permit bristles to be cut short

indicators.note: cutting a word short trims its final letter

parts.note: a beard is a growth of facial bristles

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to have their stubble trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut short' trims the last letter, D, from BEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it or tolerate it, as in 'I can't bear it', which is to permit it.

clue.text: Unpleasant drive

definitions.meaning: a drive here is a concerted attack or campaign

explanation.surface: A two-word note on a nasty journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offensive is disagreeable; an offensive is an attacking military push, a drive.

clue.text: Routine task for some Echo reporters

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Covering local events is humdrum work for journalists on the Echo newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Echo is a common name for a local newspaper; the letters run from 'eCHO' into 'REporters'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chore is a dull, routine job, a regular household or work duty.

clue.text: Cheerleaders followed by piper, turned out smartly dressed

parts.note: the leading letters of the word cheer are C and H

indicators.note: letters turned out are turned inside out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheerleaders are followed by a piper who has dressed up for the parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheerleaders' is read as 'cheer leaders': the first letters of 'cheer'. 'turned out' looks like part of 'turned out smartly', but it rearranges PIPER into IPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper means lively and cheerful, and in a dated sense neat and spruce in appearance.

clue.text: Bow-tie knotted by Ratty?

parts.note: not neckwear but the rope at a boat's bow that a riverbank rat would tie up when mooring

explanation.surface: A grumpy man fumbles with his bow tie.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty is the Water Rat in 'The Wind in the Willows', a boating enthusiast. A painter is the line at a small boat's bow used to tie it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's mooring rope at the front is called a painter, so it is a line tied at the bow.

clue.text: Coming before a superior

definitions.meaning: the head of a monastery or priory, a religious superior

explanation.surface: Someone arrives ahead of the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier in time or order; a prior is the head of a religious house, a monastic superior.

clue.text: Finished outsize cigars

parts.note: finished here means completed to the highest standard, flawless
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Someone has smoked a box of oversized cigars.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfectos are thick cigars tapered at both ends, a named shape of cigar.

clue.text: Telling of likeable rogue with grudge about troubles

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes round it

parts.note: pique is resentment from wounded pride, a grudge
cares are worries or troubles

explanation.surface: A story about a charming scoundrel nursing resentment over his difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the grudge around the troubles. 'Telling' is a noun here, a narration, not the adjective meaning revealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A picaresque novel narrates the episodic adventures of a roguish but appealing hero.

clue.text: Mum with no address?

parts.note: an address is a formal speech
the suffix -less means without, having no

explanation.surface: A mother has no home address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother but means silent, as in 'keep mum'; 'address' is a speech, not a home address.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to stay silent, unable or unwilling to say a word.

clue.text: See him changing cape, boots in cell?

definitions.text: See him changing cape, boots in cell?

indicators.note: changing means the letters of these words alter their order

explanation.surface: A man is spotted swapping his cape and boots in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges CAPE BOOTS IN CELL. As a whole the clue pictures the officer at the station, kitting out with cape and boots near the cells.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable is the lowest-ranking officer in a British police force, the uniformed beat officer.

clue.text: This stimulant could be fine in small restaurant

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the other piece

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant serving light meals

indicators.note: could be signals the word fine may be rearranged into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A strong coffee drink would be welcome in a little cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'he' is an OCR slip for 'be'. 'could be' rearranges FINE into FEIN before it goes inside the cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is the stimulant drug in coffee and tea.

clue.text: Note, every bit of space is needed for such dancing

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the adjective in 'ballroom dancing'

parts.note: B is a musical note
all means the whole, every bit
room means space, as in 'room to move'

explanation.surface: A dancing tip: plenty of space is needed for a waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with the answer as a modifier: ballroom dancing is the kind of dancing meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballroom dancing is formal partnered dancing such as the waltz and foxtrot.

clue.text: check with division for support

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a force is a body of troops, a military unit like a division

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect an army division for backup.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce something is to strengthen and support it.

clue.text: Working for business partnership that is not stable

parts.note: in means working or active, as a machine is in operation
a firm is a business, often a partnership

explanation.surface: A working partnership that turns out to be shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak or unsteady, in body or in structure.

clue.text: Cold oil-spread, with celery starter, gives one bellyache

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: spread means the letters are scattered into a new order
a starter is the first course, so the first letter of celery

explanation.surface: Cold oil spread over celery starters gives a diner stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges OIL into OLI; 'gives one' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, a bellyache, especially in babies.

clue.text: Frank Shaw's play cut

indicators.note: cut means the play's title loses its final letter

parts.note: Candida is a play by George Bernard Shaw

explanation.surface: A Shaw play is being abridged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the last A from CANDIDA. 'Frank' is the adjective, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means open and honest, speaking frankly.

clue.text: Cushions for bumbling old fellows

definitions.meaning: cushions here is a verb or noun for things that soften impact
slang for doddery, foolish old men

explanation.surface: Soft padding for dithering old men.
explanation.walkthrough: BUFFERS are the shock-absorbing stops at the end of a railway line; 'old buffer' is British slang for a doddering old man.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffers soften a blow, as cushions do; an old buffer is a fussy, foolish elderly man.

clue.text: Bishop has run amok in party

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: running amok means going wild, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A bishop goes wild at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run amok' rearranges HAS into ASH; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is an informal word for a lively party.

clue.text: After motorway, right line turns into a kingdom

definitions.note: a noun standing for the word used in 'the mineral kingdom'

indicators.note: after means the rest of the wordplay comes after the first piece

parts.note: M is a motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: turns into means the letters change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Leaving the motorway, the right lane leads into a realm.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'lane' is an OCR slip for 'line'. 'turns into' rearranges R, LINE and A into INERAL. Nature's kingdoms are animal, vegetable and mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural objects are classed into animal, vegetable and mineral realms; the mineral kingdom covers inorganic matter.

clue.text: Difficult medium

definitions.meaning: difficult here ... troublesome or tough, an informal sense
a medium here is a middle point between extremes

explanation.surface: A tricky middle way.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can be informal for tough or troublesome; a mean is a midpoint or average, a medium between extremes.

clue.text: Generator, new, that makes a loud wailing sound

definitions.text: that makes a loud wailing sound
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing which makes the sound

parts.note: a sire is a father, one who begets or generates offspring

explanation.surface: A new generator turns out to be very noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generator' looks like a machine, but it is one who generates offspring, a father or SIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a warning device producing a loud rising and falling howl.

clue.text: A Suomi nun converted as one?

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Finnish nun has changed faith along with all her sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: Suomi is Finland's name for itself, so the surface is about a Finnish nun converting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as one means everyone agreeing, which is unanimous.
